title: The Third Thing — a repair that leaves the crack visible
caption: A surveyor's working sheet rather than a surveyed country, drawn in the cartographer's hand and entered on no roll: the year is left open, for a date would want a payer under it and none stands. At the centre a clay vessel is cut open in section — walls hatched, ways cut through them, a capacity, flaws, old patches and a rate of loss — with the Warm held inside nearly full and never quite, the level a hair under the rim, and the Ash gathered in the foot as what is left when the Warm has been taken. A knuckle waits at the rim: tap a sound vessel and it answers full, a cracked one flat, and this one answers nearly full and never quite, a third sound that is neither of the first two. The flaw runs down the right wall from lip to belly and is left showing; an older brass staple crosses it and a second, tighter wire is drawn over it and left longer than it needed, while the hairline of the original break stands dark between them, for a restored thing hides the hand that handled it and a mended thing leaves that hand showing. Through the visible seam the Warm is free to move, four red arrows going out toward the cold country of the Waste, and five more rising from the Hearth below, which is drawn as a wound and not a reservoir. Beyond, three who were recalled before him are struck through in red — one made the repair beautiful and lied, one made it honest and let the world break, one became the Court — and the third thing is set apart by a dotted rule. The six ranks are drawn as small pots, Whole, Held, Drawn, Banked, Hearthward and Kept, with the note that he stops short of Kept, whose vessels hold three hundred measures and feel nothing at all. The quiet seal is forbidden here: the Court and the Unbanked want the same ending by different methods, a world in which nothing can ever be given away. Cartouche starred along its lips like the rim-seam riveted with stars, compass, a scale of a span of the wall measured in embers, a convention of signs, surveyor's notes, and in the margin the two sayings of Garl Vail, said to the pot and to the fire and never to a person — Leave the crack showing. People trust a thing they can see has been handled; and If it's worth mending it's worth mending twice. The second time is the real one.
